newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's crude ports shut, winds ebbing -captains.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's crude ports shut, winds ebbing -captains.

text.p: Mexico's three main crude ports remained shut Monday as of 1430 local/2030 GMT, officials at the ports told Reuters.
Officials at Cayo Arcas in Campeche state said the port could soon reopen as winds have died down.
At Pajaritos in Veracruz state, officials said the port could reopen later in the day, while at Dos Bocas in Tabasco state officials said the port is likely to reopen Tuesday morning.

Port officials said winds had died down to between 20 to 25 kilometers per hour from 50 kilometers per hour at Cayo Arcas, the largest of oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos' (Pemex) crude oil shipping ports. The port exports an average 600,000 barrels of crude per day, according Pemex.

At the second largest of Pemex's crude ports, Pajaritos, winds have died down to about 30 kilometers per hour, although port officials said they were still concerned about waves of up to 10 feet high.

Dos Bocas port officials said winds in the area reached 40 kilometers per hour and waves were between eight to 10 feet high. If conditions improve the port could reopen as soon as 0600 local/1200 GMT Tuesday they said.
Pemex's three main crude ports were closed on Sunday and Monday as a cold front hit the Gulf of Mexico. The ports shut after a three-day closure a week ago.
